sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: **Early Years of Freedom Movement** (Indian National Movement from **1885 to 1919**, covering the Moderate and Extremist phases)
**1885** (Formation of **Indian National Congress**) to **1919** (Government of India Act / Rowlatt Act)
Across British India, with key centers in **Bengal, Bombay, Madras, and Poona**
Foundational leaders: **A.O. Hume, W.C. Bonnerjee, Dadabhai Naoroji, Gopal Krishna Gokhale** (Moderates); **Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal, Lala Lajpat Rai, Aurobindo Ghosh** (Extremists)
Laid the institutional foundation of Indian nationalism, transformed anti-British resentment into an organized political movement, and introduced concepts like **Swaraj, Swadeshi, and Boycott**

Shift from petition-prayer-protest politics of **Moderates** to direct action, mass mobilization, and militant nationalism of **Extremists**; **Bengal Partition (1905)** and **Surat Split (1907)** as turning points
High-yield static GK area covering Congress sessions, founding years, newspaper names, partition dates, and extremist-moderate friction points frequently asked in UPSSSC exams
**Dadabhai Naoroji** propounded the **Drain of Wealth** theory in his book **'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'**; **Lord Curzon** engineered the **Partition of Bengal**

items.title: 1. Foundation of Indian National Congress (1885) and Moderate Phase
items.content:
• **Founded on:** **December 28, 1885** at **Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay**
• **First President:** **W.C. Bonnerjee** (Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee)
• **Founder Secretary:** **A.O. Hume** (Allan Octavian Hume), a retired British civil servant
• **Viceroy at Foundation:** **Lord Dufferin** (who remarked INC represented a 'microscopic minority')
• **Moderate Methods:** Called **'3Ps'** — **Prayer, Petition, and Protest**
• **Key Moderate Leaders:** **Dadabhai Naoroji, Surendranath Banerjee, Pherozeshah Mehta, Gopal Krishna Gokhale, Badruddin Tyabji**
• **Mnemonic for Moderate Leaders:** **'D-S-P-G-B'** -> **D**adabhai Naoroji, **S**urendranath Banerjee, **P**herozeshah Mehta, **G**okhale, **B**adruddin Tyabji (*'Dadabhai Secures Post Greatly By'*)

items.title: 2. Partition of Bengal (1905) and Swadeshi Movement
items.content:
• **Announcement Date:** **July 20, 1905** by **Lord Curzon**
• **Effective Date:** **October 16, 1905** (observed as a day of mourning, tying of **rakhi**, and singing **Amar Sonar Bangla** by Rabindranath Tagore)
• **Rationale Given by British:** Administrative efficiency; **Real Motive:** Divide and rule to curb the growing Bengali nationalism
• **Swadeshi and Boycott Movement:** Resolution passed in **Town Hall, Calcutta** on **August 7, 1905**
• **Spread of Movement:** **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** in Bombay and Poona, **Lala Lajpat Rai & Ajit Singh** in Punjab, **Syed Haider Raza** in Delhi, **Chidambaram Pillai** in Madras Presidency
• **Mnemonic for Swadeshi Leaders:** **'L-B-B-A'** -> **L**ala Lajpat Rai, **B**al Gangadhar Tilak, **B**ipin Chandra Pal, **A**urobindo Ghosh (*'Lal-Bal-Pal And Aurobindo'*, the Extremist quartet)

items.title: 3. Surat Split (1907) and Rise of Extremism
items.content:
• **Venue & Year:** **Surat Session, 1907** on the banks of river **Tapti**
• **Presidential Candidate Clash:** Extremists wanted **Lala Lajpat Rai** or **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**; Moderates supported **Rash Behari Ghosh**
• **Outcome:** Congress split into two factions — **Moderates** and **Extremists**
• **British Advantage:** British unleashed repression on extremists; Tilak sentenced to **6 years imprisonment** in Mandalay (Burma) in 1908
• **Mnemonic for Extremist Core:** **'LAL-BAL-PAL'** -> **L**ala Lajpat Rai, **B**al Gangadhar Tilak, **B**ipin Chandra Pal (*'Lal Bal Pal'* trio)

items.title: 4. Morley-Minto Reforms (1909) and Muslim League (1906)
items.content:
• **All-India Muslim League Founded:** **December 30, 1906** at **Dacca** by **Aga Khan, Nawab Salimullah of Dacca, and Mohsin-ul-Mulk**
• **First President of Muslim League:** **Aga Khan III**
• **Indian Councils Act 1909:** Known as **Morley-Minto Reforms** (**Lord Morley** as Secretary of State, **Lord Minto** as Viceroy)
• **Key Feature:** Introduced **Separate Electorates** for Muslims, institutionalizing communal politics in India
• **Lenin's Remark:** Described the separate electorates as sowing the dragon's teeth whose harvest was bitter

items.title: 5. Home Rule League Movement (1916)
items.content:
• **Context:** Launched during **World War I** when Indian nationalists supported Britain expecting self-government in return
• **Tilak's League:** Founded in **April 1916** at **Belgaum**; jurisdiction over Maharashtra (excluding Bombay), Karnataka, Central Provinces, and Berar; famous slogan: **'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it'**
• **Annie Besant's League:** Founded in **September 1916** at **Madras**; jurisdiction over the rest of India
• **Significance:** Reunited Moderates, Extremists (at Lucknow 1916), and Congress-Muslim League (Lucknow Pact)

items.title: 6. Lucknow Pact (1916) and Re-union
items.content:
• **Venue & Year:** **Lucknow Session, 1916**
• **Congress President:** **Ambika Charan Mazumdar**
• **Major Milestone 1:** **Extremists re-readmitted** into Congress through the efforts of **Annie Besant and Tilak**
• **Major Milestone 2:** **Lucknow Pact** signed between **INC and Muslim League**, accepting the separate electorates demand of the Muslim League
• **Significance:** Marked temporary Hindu-Muslim political unity in the freedom struggle

sections.title: Comprehensive Data Tables
rows: Founded at Bombay; A.O. Hume as secretary, W.C. Bonnerjee as first president
Announced by Lord Curzon; triggered the nationwide Swadeshi and Boycott movement
Founded in Dacca by Aga Khan and Nawab Salimullah
Congress split into Moderates and Extremists; Rash Behari Ghosh presided
Indian Councils Act introduced separate electorates for Muslims
King George V visited Delhi; Bengal Partition annulled; capital shifted from Calcutta to Delhi

'No Dalil, No Vakil, No Appeal' law giving police unbridled detention powers

items.definition: Remember the first four presidents of INC (1885, 1886, 1887, 1888): **B**onnerjee (Bombay), **N**aoroji (Calcutta), **B**adruddin Tyabji (Madras), **G**eorge Yule (Allahabad — acronym **BNBG** for **B**omber **N**aoroji **B**adruddin **G**eorge).
Remember key dates of 1905: **July 20** = Partition announced; **August 7** = Swadeshi movement launched at Calcutta Town Hall; **October 16** = Partition took effect (Rakhi day).
**L**ala Lajpat Rai = Punjab (Lion of Punjab); **B**al Gangadhar Tilak = Maharashtra (Lokmanya); **P**ipin Chandra Pal = Bengal. Remembered as the extremist Trinity.

Tilak's league started first (**April 1916**, Poona/Belgaum). Annie Besant's league started later (**September 1916**, Madras). Alphabetical order helps: **T**ilak comes before **B**esant in month sequence (April vs September).
Remember **DAD** for **D**adabhai **A**hmed/Naoroji — **D**rain of wealth book **'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'** (1901), also known as the **Grand Old Man of India**.
M-M: **M**orley was Secretary of State (in **L**ondon — longer post name), **M**into was Viceroy (in **I**ndia — shorter title).

items.term: Mistake 1: Confusing A.O. Hume and W.C. Bonnerjee
items.definition: **A.O. Hume** was the **founder/general secretary** of INC, whereas **W.C. Bonnerjee** was the **first president** of the 1885 session. Students often mix up founder with president.

items.term: Mistake 2: Date of Bengal Partition Annulment
items.definition: Bengal Partition was **announced in July 1905** and took effect in **October 1905**. However, it was **annulled in 1911** at the Delhi Darbar, not in 1908 or 1909.

items.term: Mistake 3: Surat Split vs Lucknow Pact
items.definition: The split happened at **Surat in 1907** (Congress divided), and they reunited at **Lucknow in 1916** (Congress united + Congress-League pact).

items.term: Mistake 4: First Muslim President of INC
items.definition: The first Muslim president of INC was **Badruddin Tyabji** (3rd session, Madras 1987), NOT the founders of the Muslim League (Aga Khan/Salimullah).
Muslim League was founded in **Dacca in 1906** by **Nawab Salimullah, Aga Khan III, and Mohsin-ul-Mulk**, NOT by Muhammad Ali Jinnah at its inception.
This slogan was raised by **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**, but the term 'Swaraj' as a goal was first officially used by **Dadabhai Naoroji** at the 1906 Calcutta Congress session.
Founded on **December 28, 1885** at Bombay with **W.C. Bonnerjee** as first president and **A.O. Hume** as general secretary.
Depended on **constitutional agitations, petitions, prayers, and public speeches** to press for administrative reforms.
**Dadabhai Naoroji, R.C. Dutt, and G. Subramania Iyer** exposed British economic exploitation through the **Drain of Wealth** theory.
Decided by **Lord Curzon** in **1905** on communal and administrative pretexts, leading to the massive **Swadeshi and Boycott** movement.
Led by **Lal, Bal, Pal, and Aurobindo Ghosh**, advocating self-reliance, national education, passive resistance, and complete **Swaraj**.
INC split into Moderates and Extremists at the **Surat session (1907)** over leadership and methodology disputes.
Established in **1906 at Dacca** under Nawab Salimullah and Aga Khan to safeguard Muslim political rights.
Enacted in **1909**, introducing **separate electorates** for Muslims, sowing seeds of communal division.
King George V announced the **cancellation of Bengal Partition** and the transfer of capital from **Calcutta to Delhi**.
Launched in **1916** by **Tilak and Annie Besant** to demand self-government during World War I.
Historic **1916 session** where **Moderates and Extremists reunited** and **INC-Muslim League alliance** was forged under A.C. Mazumdar.

upscNotes.content: For UPSSSC PET, memorize the exact years, founders, and session locations of INC (1885 Bombay, 1886 Calcutta, 1887 Madras, 1888 Allahabad, 1905 Varanasi, 1907 Surat, 1916 Lucknow).
Focus heavily on the newspapers started by leaders: Tilak's **Kesari** (Marathi) and **Mahratta** (English), Dadabhai Naoroji's **Rast Goftar**, and Aurobindo Ghosh's **Bande Mataram**.

UPSSSC frequently asks about who gave the 'Drain of Wealth' theory. Ensure you do not confuse Dadabhai Naoroji with R.C. Dutt (author of 'Economic History of India'). Both contributed, but Naoroji pioneered it in 1867/1901.
Watch out for trick questions regarding the Swadeshi movement date. The formal resolution was passed on **August 7, 1905**, but partition came into force on **October 16, 1905**.

keyTakeaways: INC was founded in **1885** with **A.O. Hume** as founder and **W.C. Bonnerjee** as first president.
Partition of Bengal was announced in **1905** by **Lord Curzon**, sparking the **Swadeshi and Boycott** movement.
The Congress split into Moderates and Extremists at the **Surat Session (1907)**.
All India Muslim League was established in **1906** at **Dacca** by Aga Khan and Nawab Salimullah.
**Morley-Minto Reforms (1909)** introduced **separate electorates** for Muslims for the first time.
Home Rule League movement was launched in **1916** by **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** and **Annie Besant**.
**Lucknow Pact (1916)** marked the reunion of Moderates & Extremists and political alliance between INC and Muslim League.
